title: Cassini Portable Meeting Manifest v1
description: This schema is deliberately open. Every object below accepts members it does not declare, except integrity, and a consumer MUST ignore a manifest member it does not recognise, at any depth, rather than treat its presence as an error. integrity is the exception because everything in it is an instruction for deciding whether this audio and this transcript belong together, so an unrecognised member there is a verification failure and not a lost hint. Adding a member to it is a new major version. Being open does not mean the file may be anything: every member this schema does declare keeps the type and the meaning declared here.

kind.description: The literal string that says this document is a portable meeting manifest. It does not vary, in any version of the format.

meeting.description: Open. Meeting metadata is open-ended by nature, and nothing in it is load-bearing for decoding, so a member a consumer does not recognise is ignored.

roomId.description: Id of the conversation this meeting was recorded in: a deterministic one-way derivation of the room's identity, never the identity itself. For a Nextcloud Talk recording it derives from the conversation token, which is also that room's join link and is therefore never published. Shaped rm_<16 lowercase hex>. Absent when the room is unknown.

roomName.description: LEGACY, read-only. The room's display name frozen at record time. Producers stopped writing this: a display name is editable and a published recording is not, so the current name lives in the catalog entry instead. The record-time name is still available as the meeting title. Absent in anything packed after that change.

jobId.description: Id of the operator job that produced this artifact. Absent when the producer was not an operator job. Discloses nothing new: the operator publishes the artifact under this same id.

attemptNumber.description: Which attempt of that job produced this artifact, 1-based. Absent when unknown. There is no separate attempt id: an attempt's identity is the pair (jobId, attemptNumber).

audio.description: Open. Descriptive, not instructional: it restates what the Ogg stream already says, so a consumer that ignores a member it does not recognise loses nothing.

integrity.description: CLOSED. A member here that a consumer does not recognise is a verification failure and not a hint: a consumer that ignored an unrecognised digest field would report a file as verified while ignoring the field that defines its identity. Adding a member to this object is a new major version, and that is the deliberate price of the open-world rule everywhere else.

items.description: Open. The two-string speaker is deliberate, but a colour or an external identity is a hint and not an instruction, so a member a consumer does not recognise is ignored.

transcript.description: Open. The inline body of a v1 file, the same shape a v2 or v3 chunk set carries. spec/cassini-words-v1.schema.json describes that body and is open, and this must not disagree with it.

items.description: Open. Per-word annotations get added over time: attributionGapDb and lowConfidenceSpeaker were each exactly that. A consumer ignores what it does not recognise.

provenance.description: Open. A new kind of provenance is the likeliest addition of all: meetingSummary, attribution and wordTimings were each exactly that in later versions, and each cost a version bump under a closed schema.

displayTranscript.description: Optional derived view for rendering, transcript.display.v1. Present in every shipped v1 file; declared here because the closed root would otherwise reject them.

items.description: Open. endMs was added at v2 and made every v1 chapter that already carried it invalid, which is the bug this rule exists to prevent.

processingStep.description: Open. Every member is optional and every member is a note about how one stage ran, so a consumer ignores what it does not recognise.
